Ghost-Machine · Drowned Coast · The Manifest's Reddest Entry

Before the Turning, it was a mobile debt-collection walker — a legged crane-rig an Aristocratic Republic's tax authority used to physically repossess property from defaulters who couldn't be reasoned with by mail. When the firebombing came, its operating crew and a firebombed block's worth of foreclosed debtors' souls fused into its boiler at once, all in the same few seconds, all still owing the same unpayable balance.

It still works its old route through the Drowned Coast, foreclosing on ruins that have had no owner in two centuries, dragging away scrap, salvage, and the occasional unlucky scavenger toward a debt that was already meaningless before the world ended. Bolted into its chest is a literal ledger-book, fused to the chassis, its balance always reading a figure that can never reach zero — and a petty god, known as the Ledger, is rumored to slip it fresh entries out of pure amusement, just to watch it try.

A full chapter of Circuit riders — the Nine of Redlake — went in to Name and re-bind it thirty years back. One rider came out. Her final charm-scrawled account of what went wrong is copied into every new Wardbreaker's training packet, under a title that's become Circuit shorthand for overreach: never let it total you.

TABLE USE — a high-level, near-unkillable hazard encounter or long-form pursuit; its Anchor (the unpayable ledger entry) can theoretically be Named and Broken, but doing so has never once been done cleanly.
